C1.statement: The pool is a golang universal network connection pool.
C1.fragment: A golang universal network connection pool.

C2.statement: The connection type in the connection pool is interface{}, making it more versatile.
C2.fragment: The connection type in the connection pool is `interface{}`, making it more versatile

C3.statement: The connection supports setting the maximum idle time.
C3.fragment: The connection supports setting the maximum idle time

C4.statement: The timeout connection will be closed and discarded.
C4.fragment: the timeout connection will be closed and discarded

C5.statement: Setting the maximum idle time can avoid the problem of automatic connection failure when idle.

C10.statement: When the connection pool is full, it supports connection waiting (like the go db connection pool).
C10.fragment: When the connection pool is full, support for connection waiting (like the go db connection pool)

C11.statement: The factory specifies the method to create the connection.
C11.fragment: factory Specify the method to create the connection

C12.statement: The close function specifies the method to close the connection.
C12.fragment: close Specify the method to close the connection

C13.statement: The ping function specifies the method to detect whether the connection is invalid.
C13.fragment: ping Specify the method to detect whether the connection is invalid

C14.statement: InitialCap initializes the number of connections to 5.
C14.fragment: Initialize the number of connections to 5

C15.statement: MaxIdle is the maximum idle connection, set to 20.

C16.statement: MaxCap is the maximum concurrent connection, set to 30.

C17.statement: IdleTimeout is the maximum idle time of the connection.
C17.fragment: The maximum idle time of the connection

C18.statement: The connection exceeding the idle time will be closed.
C18.fragment: the connection exceeding this time will be closed

C19.statement: The maximum idle time can avoid the problem of automatic failure when connecting to EOF when idle.

C20.statement: The pool is created with pool.NewChannelPool(poolConfig).

C21.statement: Get gets a connection from the connection pool.
C21.fragment: Get a connection from the connection pool

C22.statement: The connection is retrieved from the pool via p.Get().

C23.statement: The connection is put back into the connection pool when the connection is no longer in use.
C23.fragment: Put the connection back into the connection pool, when the connection is no longer in use

C24.statement: The connection is returned via p.Put(v).

C25.statement: Release releases all connections in the connection pool when resources need to be destroyed.
C25.fragment: Release all connections in the connection pool, when resources need to be destroyed

C27.statement: Len views the number of connections in the current connection pool.
C27.fragment: View the number of connections in the current connection pool

C28.statement: The current number of connections is obtained via p.Len().

questions: What happens when Get is called and the pool is full and no connection is available — does it block, wait, or return an error?
How long does a caller wait for a connection when the pool is full?
Is there a timeout for waiting for a connection, and can it be configured?
Does Get validate a connection before returning it (e.g., via ping), or is ping only used on Put/return?
When exactly is ping called — on Get, on Put, periodically, or another time?
What happens to a connection when ping returns an error?
What is the default behavior if Ping is not configured?
Is InitialCap a minimum number of connections maintained at all times, or only the initial number created at pool construction?
How does MaxIdle relate to MaxCap and InitialCap — what happens to idle connections beyond MaxIdle?
What happens when Put is called and the number of idle connections would exceed MaxIdle?
Does Put close connections beyond MaxIdle?
Is IdleTimeout checked on Get, on Put, periodically, or another time?
What happens to a connection retrieved by Get that has exceeded IdleTimeout?
What happens if Get returns an error — is the caller returned a nil connection?
What does Release do to connections currently checked out by callers?
Does the pool remain usable after Release is called?
Does Len count idle connections only, in-use connections only, or both?
Is MaxCap a hard limit on total connections created, or only on concurrent connections?
What happens if Factory returns an error during pool creation or connection creation?
Is the pool thread-safe / safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines?
What does NewChannelPool return as error, and when does it fail?
Does the pool reopen or recreate connections after Release?
Is there any ordering guarantee between Put returning a connection and a waiting Get receiving it?
What happens to a connection if the caller never calls Put after Get?
